title: Queen of Two Thrones
tagline: She led armies, negotiated empires, and never surrendered Angola.

scenes.text: Angola, 1622. Portuguese colonizers hold Luanda and push inland, enslaving thousands. The Kingdom of Ndongo needs a negotiator — and Queen Anna Nzinga will not kneel.
At the peace talks, the Portuguese offer no chair for her. Nzinga signals to one of her attendants, who kneels — and she sits on the attendant's back. She will not be lesser.

challenge.instruction: No chair is offered, so Nzinga makes a seat of her attendant and treats as the governor's equal. Choose the terms that enough of the room in Luanda will sign without Ndongo kneeling to Portugal.
challenge.fact: In 1622 Nzinga persuaded Governor João Correia de Sousa to treat Ndongo as an ally rather than a tributary vassal, and was baptised in Luanda as Dona Ana de Sousa. She used the faith as diplomacy: years later she returned to her own religion, then accepted Christianity again in the 1650s to make peace with Portugal.

scenes.text: The Portuguese break the treaty. Nzinga retreats east, conquers Matamba, and builds a new base of power — welcoming escaped slaves and Imbangala warriors.

challenge.instruction: Matamba's markets will pay for Nzinga's new kingdom and its army. Buy raffia cloth when the news drives it cheap and sell when war and shortage drive it dear.
challenge.fact: Driven out of Ndongo, Nzinga conquered the kingdom of Matamba around 1631 and made it her base, welcoming runaway slaves and allying with Imbangala war bands. Matamba grew rich on trade — above all, grimly, the sale of war captives to European slavers.

scenes.text: For decades she fights on — allying with the Dutch, leading armies personally, and negotiating across three colonial powers. She rules until her 80s, never truly conquered.

challenge.instruction: With the Dutch now holding Luanda, Nzinga must join her war camps to her new allies' posts. Link every camp across the rivers so the alliance can move as one army.
challenge.fact: After the Dutch seized Luanda in 1641, Nzinga allied with them against Portugal. In 1647 her army and Dutch troops routed the Portuguese at Kombi and besieged the fort of Massangano, until a Portuguese fleet from Brazil retook Luanda in 1648.

scenes.text: She even negotiates the release of Portuguese prisoners, turning each crisis into leverage. Her diplomacy is as deadly as her sword.

challenge.instruction: Nzinga knew the rivers of Ndongo better than any Portuguese captain. Run the war canoe down the Kwanza to the island stronghold, steering clear of rocks, hippos and crocodiles.
challenge.fact: Nzinga's forces moved by river and forest, striking Portuguese supply lines and vanishing before columns could react. The guerrilla war she waged kept the Portuguese out of her kingdom of Matamba for decades, until a 1656 treaty finally recognised her as its queen.

scenes.text: Anna Nzinga dies in 1663, still queen, still free. Her name becomes a symbol of African resistance against colonialism for centuries to come.

challenge.instruction: Lead Nzinga's forces in a flanking raid against a Portuguese supply column. Speed and terrain are your weapons — European cannon cannot aim at what it cannot see.
challenge.fact: Portuguese military reports describe Nzinga's forces as extraordinarily mobile and difficult to engage in pitched battle. She understood that her army could not match European firepower in open confrontation, so she avoided it — choosing ambushes, river crossings, and night raids that neutralized the Portuguese advantage.

params.title: The Siege of Massangano, 1647
params.intro: After routing the Portuguese at Kombi, Nzinga and her Dutch allies close on the river fort of Massangano, but the garrison has sown the approaches with buried powder charges. Open every safe square; each number counts the charges in the eight squares around it.
params.fact: In October 1647 Nzinga and her Dutch allies routed a Portuguese army at Kombi and laid siege to Massangano, the last Portuguese stronghold inland. The fort held out: in August 1648 Salvador Correia de Sá retook Luanda from the Dutch, and Nzinga had to withdraw to Matamba.

challenge.instruction: Her greatest campaign brings Nzinga to the walls of Massangano. Clear a safe way through the Portuguese defences without setting off a single charge.
challenge.fact: In October 1647 Nzinga and her Dutch allies routed a Portuguese army at Kombi and laid siege to Massangano, the last Portuguese stronghold inland. The fort held out: in August 1648 Salvador Correia de Sá retook Luanda from the Dutch, and Nzinga had to withdraw to Matamba.

scenes.speaker: Anna Nzinga
scenes.text: Two face-down cards: one at St Petersburg, one at London. We cannot see who they are until we attack, and an attack reveals every card at the location. The Coup already runs at St Petersburg; you hold a card to start one at London.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 5 · Face Down. Win two attacks: fight at St Petersburg where the Coup is running, then carry the fight to London by starting your own event there.
challenge.fact: A card on the board can be public (face up) or private (face down). A private card hides its identity and stats from rivals until an attack reveals every card at that location. Your own cards deploy face down; Toggle Public when being seen helps you.
